LOCAL-FIRST DEPLOYMENT ANALYZER

Know what's broken before you ship.

ShipCheck runs rule-based checks against your local codebase — catching security issues, broken builds, misconfiguration, and deployment risks. Every finding is weighted toward a single Ship Score and stays on your machine.

Features

Rule-based checks across your repository with weights that reflect real deployment risk.

Configuration Analysis

Validates deployment configs, environment setup, and project structure against common production requirements.

Dependency Checks

Runs npm audit and inspects dependencies for known issues, with results tied to the weighted Ship Score.

Security Analysis

Scans for secrets, verifies .env.example coverage, and flags risky patterns without sending data off-machine.

Code Quality

Runs ESLint against your project config to catch code quality issues as part of the weighted score.

Secret Detection

Performs local regex-based secret scanning and checks for missing .env.example coverage.

Git Analysis

Checks branch, working tree status, and .gitignore presence to catch common repository issues.

How It Works

ShipCheck uses two terminals: one runs the local server, the other initialises and scans your project.

01

Start the local server

Open your project directory in a terminal and start the ShipCheck server. Keep this terminal running while you use the CLI — it hosts the local dashboard and prints its URL.

> npx shipcheck-cli07 server
02

Initialise your project

Without closing the server terminal, open a new terminal window or tab. Navigate to the same project directory and initialise ShipCheck with the running server.

> npx shipcheck-cli07 init
03

Run the scan

Continue in the second terminal. Run the scan to analyse your repository locally. Open the dashboard URL printed in the terminal to review your Ship Score and findings.

> npx shipcheck-cli07 scan

Documentation / Getting Started

Install, initialize, and scan from the CLI. After a scan, review findings and suggested fixes in the local dashboard or CLI output.

TERMINAL 1 Start the ShipCheck server

Open PowerShell or your preferred terminal in your project directory. Run the following command. Keep this terminal open while using ShipCheck.

PowerShell 
npx shipcheck-cli07 server
Expected output 
ShipCheck server is running.

Dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:3140/?token=<token>

Important: Do not close this terminal. The local server must remain running while the CLI communicates with it.

TERMINAL 2 Register your project and run a scan

Open a new terminal window or tab. Navigate to the same project directory where you ran the server command. Do not open a different project folder.

PowerShell 
npx shipcheck-cli07 init

Registers your current project with the running ShipCheck server. This is generally required when setting up a project for the first time.

PowerShell 
npx shipcheck-cli07 scan

Analyses your project and generates the Ship Score and issue findings.

Example result 
SHIPCHECK

Project       shipcheck
SHIP SCORE    92/100
STATUS        READY

Scan completed successfully.

This is illustrative output only — your actual score and status will vary.

Run both commands in Terminal 2. Keep Terminal 1 running.

Prefer a globally installed CLI?

Install ShipCheck once to use the shipcheck-cli07 command without prefixing it with npx.

PowerShell 
npm install -g shipcheck-cli07

After installation, the workflow is the same — only how you invoke the CLI changes:

Terminal 1 
shipcheck-cli07 server
Terminal 2 
shipcheck-cli07 init
shipcheck-cli07 scan

Global installation changes only how the CLI is invoked. It does not eliminate the need for two terminals.

Optional: set SHIPCHECK_PASSWORD to secure your local dashboard. Add --deploy-url to init for post-deployment checks. Findings include severity and suggested fixes to guide remediation.
